clue.text: In South Germany, sailors on Rhine perhaps delivering drink

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another means it is placed inside the pair of letters around it

blocks.note: S is the compass abbreviation for south
the sailors manning a ship are its crew
D is the international vehicle code for Germany (Deutschland)
the Rhine is an example of a river, hence 'perhaps'

explanation.surface: Boatmen on the Rhine in southern Germany are bringing drinks to someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In South Germany' reads as a location, but South and Germany are two single letters that hold the sailors between them. D for Germany comes from international car registration plates.
explanation.definitionFit: A screwdriver is a cocktail of vodka and orange juice, so it is one example of a mixed alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: South European peninsula where it snows a lot

blocks.note: S is the compass abbreviation for south
Iberia is the peninsula holding Spain and Portugal

explanation.surface: A sunny southern European peninsula is oddly described as a place of heavy snowfall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South European peninsula' reads as one description of Iberia itself, but South gives only its S, and the snowy place is a different region entirely.
explanation.definitionFit: Siberia, the vast Russian region east of the Urals, is famous for long, bitterly cold winters with plenty of snowfall.

clue.text: A little water moving penny down drain, runs over penny

indicators.note: taking one letter of a word and shifting it further along sends the front letter to the back

blocks.note: taken as written; its first letter is the old penny, d
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over
P is the abbreviation for a modern penny

explanation.surface: A trickle of water carries a coin down the plughole.
explanation.walkthrough: Penny appears twice: first as d, the abbreviation for an old pre-decimal penny, which moves down DRAIN to give RAIND; then as p, the modern penny, at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A raindrop is a single small drop of water falling from the sky, a tiny quantity of liquid.

clue.text: Raising fuss, namby-pambies

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting something upward makes it read from bottom to top

blocks.note: to be in a stew is to be in a state of fuss or agitation

explanation.surface: Feeble, timid people kicking up a fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raising fuss' looks like a phrase meaning making a fuss; in this down entry it means writing the fuss word upward. In British usage a wet is a weak, ineffectual person.
explanation.definitionFit: A wet in British slang is a feeble, spineless person, which matches the sense of a weak and timid character.

clue.text: About A Boy: accomplished, wise

blocks.note: re means about or concerning
taken as written
a son is a boy child
an able person is accomplished or skilled

explanation.surface: A critic sums up the Nick Hornby novel About a Boy as accomplished and wise.
explanation.walkthrough: The italics dress the first three words as a book title (Nick Hornby's novel), but they split into three separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A reasonable person shows sound judgement and good sense, which is close in meaning to being sensible or sagacious.

clue.text: On radio, covers glens

indicators.note: radio is heard rather than seen, so the word is judged by its sound

blocks.note: veils are light coverings, for a face or anything else

explanation.surface: A radio broadcast reports on Scottish glens.
explanation.walkthrough: Covers are veils, and veils and the target word are pronounced the same in most accents.
explanation.definitionFit: A vale and a glen are both poetic or regional terms for a valley, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Most of wine and spirits Everyman imbibed, needing healthier routine

indicators.note: most but not all of a word means its final letter is dropped
to imbibe is to drink in, so one piece is swallowed inside another

blocks.note: red is a kind of wine
gin is a spirit
the setter, Everyman, refers to himself as me

explanation.surface: The setter, having drunk plenty of wine and spirits, needs a healthier way of living.
explanation.walkthrough: RE(d) is followed by GIN holding ME. A setter's own pen name in a clue stands for me or I.
explanation.definitionFit: A regimen is a prescribed course of diet, exercise or treatment intended to improve health, so it is a healthier routine.

clue.text: Chinese weaned off dairy and booze

indicators.note: food that has gone off is spoiled, so the letters are spoiled into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Chinese people are being weaned off dairy products and alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weaned off' reads naturally as one phrasal verb, but 'off' is working alone as the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheese is a dairy product and wine is an alcoholic drink, so the pairing names both items in reverse order.

clue.text: Invitation to gratification in seedy São Paulo resort

indicators.note: read as re-sort, it asks for the letters to be sorted again into another order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged, accent ignored

explanation.surface: A sleazy Brazilian holiday resort offers its visitors indulgence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resort' looks like a noun completing the picture of a holiday destination, but it is the verb re-sort, telling you to rearrange the preceding letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase permits someone to follow their own wishes, so it invites them to indulge themselves freely.

clue.text: Endless nubility vigorously essential

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is cut off
something shaken vigorously is thrown about, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the word with its last letter removed

explanation.surface: Someone insists that boundless youthful attractiveness is absolutely necessary.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the y from the long word, then rearrange the seven letters left.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inbuilt is an inherent, integral part of a thing, which is one sense of being essential to its nature.

clue.text: Primarily, a Latinate locution expressly gainsaying ritenuto, orchestrally!

definitions.text: Primarily, a Latinate locution expressly gainsaying ritenuto, orchestrally!

indicators.note: primary things come first, so only the opening letter of each word counts

blocks.clueFragment: a Latinate locution expressly gainsaying ritenuto, orchestrally
blocks.note: the initial letters of these seven words

explanation.surface: A pompous description of a musical term that contradicts holding back the tempo.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does double duty: its initials spell the answer, and read as a sentence it describes the term. Ritenuto is the Italian marking for holding back the pace, and allegro asks for the opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: Allegro is an Italian score marking telling players to perform quickly and briskly, the reverse of slowing down.

clue.text: Sinned a little, altogether redeemable

indicators.note: only a small part of the following words is wanted, a run of letters inside them

blocks.note: the run of letters spans the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: Someone who transgressed only slightly can be completely redeemed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sinned a little' reads as a mild confession, but 'a little' points into the words that follow: altogeth-ER RED-eemable.
explanation.definitionFit: To err is to make a mistake or do wrong, and in the religious sense that is to commit a sin.

clue.text: Disposes of Tories with hesitant utterances about Europe

indicators.note: going around something means wrapping it, so one piece encloses another

blocks.note: Cons is short for Conservatives, the Tory party
um is the sound people make when hesitating
E is the abbreviation for Europe

explanation.surface: Voters get rid of the Conservatives, who keep stammering about Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: Tories are members of Britain's Conservative Party, informally the Cons. 'Disposes of' suggests throwing away, but here it means using up.
explanation.definitionFit: To consume food or resources is to use them up or eat them, which is a sense of getting rid of them.

clue.text: Agreeing it's dear to acquire distressed denim

indicators.note: distressed fabric is deliberately worn and roughed up, so the letters are knocked out of order
to acquire something is to take it in, so one piece ends up held within another

blocks.note: something dear to you is something liked
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Two people concur that buying distressed jeans is expensive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dear' looks like it means expensive, with denim the costly item; instead 'it's dear' means it is liked, and the jumbled denim sits inside that word.
explanation.definitionFit: Like-minded people share opinions and tastes, so they are in agreement or accord with one another.

clue.text: Ice-cream option, on plate, in a shambles

indicators.note: a shambles is a complete mess, so the letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A dessert choice served on a plate arrives in a messy state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a' looks like part of the phrase 'in a shambles', but those two words are letters to be rearranged along with 'on plate'.
explanation.definitionFit: Neapolitan ice cream is the familiar block of strawberry, vanilla and chocolate stripes, one of the flavour choices offered.

clue.text: Data derived from rainforests

indicators.note: something drawn out of a source comes from within it, a run of its letters

blocks.note: the run of letters sits inside the word

explanation.surface: Scientific facts are gathered from tropical jungles.
explanation.walkthrough: The word is tucked inside the long word: ra-INFO-rests.
explanation.definitionFit: Info is the informal short form of information, and data is facts or information gathered together.

clue.text: Quiet Greek regularly strips off, gets ready

indicators.note: at regular intervals means every other letter is kept

blocks.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
the second and fourth letters
to pare is to trim or strip off an outer layer

explanation.surface: A quiet Greek methodically undresses and gets himself ready.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strips off' sounds like undressing, but here it is a verb meaning peels or trims away.
explanation.definitionFit: To prepare is to make oneself or something ready in advance, so prepares and gets ready are direct synonyms.

clue.text: Workers get benefits in this cage

blocks.note: first meaning: a cooperative, a business owned by its members who share the profits
second meaning: an enclosure for keeping poultry

explanation.surface: Employees feel trapped by their perks, as if kept in a cage.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen splits the first sense from the second: written with a hyphen it is the business, without it the enclosure for hens.
explanation.definitionFit: A co-operative shares profits among member employees, while a coop is an enclosure for chickens or other birds.

clue.text: Bit of drama in early part of Bible: well, well!

blocks.note: OT is the Old Testament, the first part of the Bible
hello is an exclamation of surprise, like well, well

explanation.surface: A surprised reaction to a dramatic episode early in the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hello, hello!' or 'hello' alone is a British exclamation of surprised discovery, like 'well, well'.
explanation.definitionFit: Othello is a tragedy by Shakespeare, so it is one play from the body of dramatic literature, a modest understatement.

clue.text: Dutch society procuring English beer runs joint franchise

indicators.note: to procure is to obtain and take in, so the outer pair gets something placed between them

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for Dutch
E is the abbreviation for English
ale is a kind of beer
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs
S is the abbreviation for society
the hip is a joint of the body

explanation.surface: A Dutch company acquires an English brewery and runs a shared franchise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dutch society' is a single letter each, wrapped around the English beer and runs. 'Joint' looks like an adjective for the franchise, but it is a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: A dealership is a business licensed to sell a particular company's products, which is what a franchise authorises.

clue.text: With time being taken, dashed over hazard, ultimately!

indicators.note: one letter is taken away and another arrives in its place
the ultimate letter is the last one of the preceding word

blocks.note: to hurtle is to rush or dash at speed
T is the abbreviation for time
the final letter

explanation.surface: A runner, against the clock, sprinted over an obstacle at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the T out of HURTLED and let D, the last letter of hazard, fill its spot. The definition reuses words from the wordplay, so the clue partly reads as its own description.
explanation.definitionFit: To hurdle is to jump over an obstacle while running, so a runner who did so dashed across a barrier.

clue.text: Country's leaderless state shown in film; not, oddly, optimal

indicators.note: without a leader means the opening letter is removed
keeping what is not in the odd positions leaves only the even-numbered letters

blocks.note: E.T. is the Spielberg film about an extraterrestrial
Ohio is a US state; it loses its first letter
the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: A film depicts a country without a ruler, and things there are far from ideal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not, oddly' reads as a comment, but it tells you to discard the odd-position letters of the following word, keeping the even ones. The film is Spielberg's 1982 alien classic.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethiopia is a nation in the Horn of Africa, so it is a straightforward example of a sovereign state.

clue.text: Part of nibbles: I'm surprised the French including starters of inedible veloutés

indicators.note: the starter of each word is its opening letter
to include something is to hold it within, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: O is an exclamation of surprise
le is a French word for the
the opening letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A diner is shocked that the French snacks come with cream soups nobody can eat.
explanation.walkthrough: A velouté is a smooth, creamy French sauce or soup; only the initials of the last two words are used, and they sit inside the French article.
explanation.definitionFit: Olives are a classic savoury snack set out with drinks, so one is a single item among the nibbles.

clue.text: In itself, Money Bag #1, so to speak!

indicators.note: speaking means saying the word out, so it is identified by its pronunciation

blocks.note: a purse is a small bag for money; #1 marks the first such bag

explanation.surface: A self-important claim about some leading money bag, considered on its own terms.
explanation.walkthrough: A small bag for coins, said out loud, is heard as the two-word Latin phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Per se is Latin for by or through itself, used in English to mean intrinsically or in itself.

clue.text: Then going in Jack's direction, finding giant

indicators.note: Jack climbed the beanstalk, so in a down clue the word travels upward and reads bottom to top

blocks.note: ergo is Latin for therefore, then

explanation.surface: A fairy-tale scene: climbing after Jack, someone comes upon the giant.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack and the Beanstalk supplies the direction: Jack goes up, so the word is written upward in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogre is a man-eating giant of folklore, like the one who lives at the top of the beanstalk.

clue.text: Ill-used, warped, depraved

indicators.note: something warped is twisted out of shape, so the letters are bent into a different arrangement

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged, hyphen ignored

explanation.surface: Three adjectives for someone mistreated, twisted and corrupt.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue looks like a list of three near-synonyms; only the last is the definition, the first is the material and the middle one the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Sullied means tainted or morally soiled, which is close to corrupted or debased, the sense of depraved here.

clue.text: Makes corrupt run for money in sweepstakes?

indicators.note: one thing standing for another means it replaces it in the word

blocks.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for run
M is the abbreviation for money, as in M1 or M3
a sweepstake is a gamble, a lottery on a race; the question mark admits the stretch

explanation.surface: Fixing a sweepstake by swapping in a runner for cash is corruption.
explanation.walkthrough: In GAMBLES the M gives way to R. M for money is the economists' label for money supply measures.
explanation.definitionFit: To garble a message is to distort or jumble it, so that its text becomes corrupted or unreadable.

clue.text: Prepared salad to follow balls – too fancy?

indicators.note: one thing following another means it is placed after it in the word

blocks.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled
a salad is prepared by adding dressing

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a salad served after the meatballs is too elaborate.
explanation.walkthrough: Balls looks like food beside the salad, but it is cricket: an over is six balls delivered by one bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: Being overdressed is wearing clothes too formal or elaborate for an occasion; the question mark flags this as a slightly loose sense.
